title: Stop bleeding
lead: Call 911 first if you have any signal.
source: Stop the Bleed guidance and ATP 3-50.21

steps.title: Press hard
steps.body: Put cloth or gauze on the wound and push down firmly with both hands. Do not lift to check.

steps.title: Arm or leg still bleeding?
steps.body: Apply a tourniquet 2–3 inches above the wound, not on a joint. Tighten until bleeding stops.

steps.title: Note the time
steps.body: Write the time the tourniquet went on. Do not loosen it.

steps.title: Wound on body or neck?
steps.body: Pack it tightly with gauze or clean cloth, then keep pressing until help arrives.

title: CPR for an adult
lead: Hands-only CPR, for a teen or adult who suddenly collapses. Call 911 on speaker.
source: American Heart Association hands-only CPR and American Red Cross first aid guidance

steps.title: Check and call
steps.body: Tap the shoulder and shout. If there is no response and no normal breathing, call 911 and put the phone on speaker.

steps.title: Hands on the chest
steps.body: Place the heel of one hand in the center of the chest, your other hand on top, fingers laced. Keep your arms straight.

steps.title: Push hard and fast
steps.body: Push straight down at least 2 inches, 100 to 120 times a minute. Let the chest come all the way back up between pushes.

steps.title: Do not stop
steps.body: Keep going until the person moves and breathes, or until someone takes over. Swap with another person every two minutes if you can.

steps.title: Use an AED when it arrives
steps.body: Turn it on and follow the spoken instructions. Restart compressions as soon as it tells you to.

title: Make water safe
lead: Boiling is the surest way. Use bleach only when you cannot boil.
source: CDC: Making Water Safe in an Emergency; EPA emergency disinfection of drinking water

steps.title: Clear it first
steps.body: Let cloudy water settle, then pour it through a clean cloth, paper towel or coffee filter.

steps.title: Boil if you can
steps.body: Bring it to a rolling boil for 1 minute. Above 6,500 feet, boil for 3 minutes. Let it cool on its own.

steps.title: No heat? Use plain bleach
steps.body: Per gallon of clear water, add 8 drops of unscented 6% household bleach, or 6 drops of 8.25%. Stir well.

steps.title: Wait 30 minutes
steps.body: The water should smell faintly of bleach. If it does not, repeat the dose and wait another 15 minutes.

steps.title: Store it covered
steps.body: Keep treated water in clean, covered containers out of sunlight.

title: Hypothermia
lead: Call 911. Shivering that stops on its own is a bad sign, not a good one.
source: CDC guidance on hypothermia and cold stress

steps.title: Know the signs
steps.body: Adults: shivering, slurred speech, clumsy hands, confusion, drowsiness. Babies: bright red, cold skin and very low energy.

steps.title: Get out of the cold
steps.body: Move the person into a warm room or shelter. Handle them gently and keep them lying still.

steps.title: Take off wet clothes
steps.body: Remove anything wet and dry the skin.

steps.title: Warm the middle first
steps.body: Cover the chest, neck, head and groin with blankets, or use skin-to-skin contact under a blanket. Do not rub the arms and legs.

steps.title: Warm drinks only if fully awake
steps.body: Give warm, sweet, non-alcoholic drinks. Never give alcohol, and never give anything to someone who cannot swallow.

steps.title: Keep them covered
steps.body: Once they start to warm, wrap the whole body including the head and keep them still until help arrives.

title: Signal for help
lead: Text instead of calling — short messages get through when calls do not.
source: FEMA / Ready.gov guidance on communicating during a disaster

steps.title: Text, do not call
steps.body: Send a short text. Voice calls tie up the networks that emergency crews need.

steps.title: Save your battery
steps.body: Turn on low-power mode, dim the screen and close everything you are not using.

steps.title: Tell your out-of-area contact
steps.body: Message the contact in your plan and let them pass the word on to everyone else.

steps.title: Make yourself seen and heard
steps.body: Three of anything means distress: three whistle blasts, three flashes, three fires. Use a mirror or bright cloth by day.

steps.title: Stay where you are if you can
steps.body: Rescuers search last known locations. If you must move, leave a note saying where you are going and when you left.

title: Shelter in place
lead: Get inside, stay inside, stay tuned.
source: FEMA / Ready.gov shelter-in-place guidance; CDC carbon monoxide guidance

steps.title: Get everyone inside
steps.body: Bring people and pets in. Lock the doors and close the windows, vents and fireplace damper.

steps.title: Pick an interior room
steps.body: Choose a small room with as few windows as possible, and take your kit and radio with you.

steps.title: Turn off air movement
steps.body: Shut off fans, heating and air conditioning so outside air is not pulled in.

steps.title: Seal the room only if told to
steps.body: If officials report a chemical or radiological release, tape plastic sheeting over the doors, windows and vents of that room.

steps.title: Listen for the all-clear
steps.body: Keep a battery or hand-crank radio on NOAA Weather Radio and wait for officials to say it is safe.

steps.title: Never burn fuel indoors
steps.body: No generator, grill or camp stove inside, in a garage or near a window. Carbon monoxide has no smell and kills.
